newsitem.title: UK: British all-women team reaches North Pole.
newsitem.headline: British all-women team reaches North Pole.

text.p: A group of British women reached the North Pole on Tuesday in the first all-female expedition to successfully cross the Arctic ice-cap, organisers said.
The 20 women, ranging in age from 21 to 51 pulled their own sledges across the 1,000 km journey in relay teams of five.
The final team reached the North Pole at 0345 GMT on Monday, ending a walk which started in northern Canada on March 14.
"It is a fantastic achievment. They have done this through sheer will-power and determination," said operations manager Mike Ewart-Smith.

The women, who include journalists, physiotherapists and designers, were selected from a group of 100 applicants who went through rigorous fitness and endurance trials in Britain last year after replying to a newspaper advertisement.
"The concept was to enable women from all sorts of walks of life to achieve a fantastic goal but at the same time carry on their own lives," said Ewart-Smith.
"Team work has played a major part in their success. The women have all been looking after themselves and each other," he added.
He said all the women were fit and well, with the only major incident being one woman who suffered a dislocated shoulder.

The women were split into five teams walking in stages ranging from 70 to 110 miles (40 to 70 km). They pulled sledges of equipment and supplies weighing 120 pounds (55 pounds) over terrain ranging from ice-pressure ridges to cracking ice sea.
"One of the most amazing things is that all of the teams has emerged looking as though they have merely been on a healthy walk in the English Lake District," Ewart-Smith said.
